headline: Minneapolis Mayor Jacob Frey has vetoed a city law that would have required a human driver in every robotaxi.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a real new step in a local robotaxi fight, but limited to one city.
importance_line: Riders, including people with disabilities the mayor cited, keep access to driverless rides for now, while the drivers the council wanted to protect lose that safeguard; the council could still override or rewrite the law.
summary: CBS News reports that Frey vetoed the ordinance on Friday, a day after the City Council passed it 7 to 6, calling it a “back door ban” that ignores issues such as emergency response, privacy and insurance. New today: the veto itself; the council needs nine votes to override it, but only seven members voted for the ordinance.
notes: Follow-up of yesterday’s item on the council vote of 1 Oct 2026 and Frey’s promise to veto. Full article read.
